title: Review: Alkanes, fuels and cracking; Combustion and fuels
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR06#t3 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t4 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN11#N.15, OR06#N.11, EN11#N.3, OR06#N.4, EN11#N.5, OR06#N.17, EN11#N.8, OR06#N.14. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Soot
items.clue: The solid C that can form when an alkane burns in limited oxygen.

items.label: Complete combustion
items.clue: Burning in plenty of O₂, so that all C ends as CO₂ and all H as H₂O.

items.label: Haemoglobin
items.clue: Binds CO more strongly than oxygen, so the blood carries less oxygen.

items.label: Carbon monoxide
items.clue: Colourless, odourless, toxic gas formed when a fuel burns in limited oxygen.

questions.stem: After cooking outdoors, campers carry a still-glowing charcoal barbecue into their closed tent for warmth. Charcoal is almost pure carbon. Why is this deadly, even though there is no flame?

options.text: The charcoal burns to extra carbon dioxide, C + O₂ → CO₂, which binds to haemoglobin in place of oxygen.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, an acidic gas that damages the lungs.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, which binds to haemoglobin.
The charcoal uses up all of the oxygen in the tent, and this lack of oxygen suffocates the campers.

questions.stem: Methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen. Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: In a very limited supply of oxygen the carbon is deposited as soot, while the hydrogen still forms water. 1 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: When the equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈, is balanced with a coefficient of 2 for octane, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ forms 16CO₂ and 18H₂O, which contain 16 × 2 + 18 = 50 O atoms. Each O₂ supplies two O atoms, so 25 O₂ are needed.

questions.stem: Which alkane has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Longest chain and unbranched: most electrons and most surface contact, so the strongest forces between molecules (bp 69 °C).

questions.stem: What amount of oxygen, O₂, is needed to burn 0.500 mol of propan-1-ol, C₃H₇OH, completely?
questions.explanation: C₃H₇OH + 4½O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The products contain 10 O atoms; the alcohol supplies 1, so O₂ supplies 9: 4½ O₂ per mole. 0.500 × 4.5 = 2.25 mol.

questions.stem: A gas heater burns methane in a small room. The window is shut and the air vent is blocked. Why is this dangerous?

options.text: Methane burns completely, and the carbon dioxide that forms is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so CO forms, which cuts the oxygen that blood can carry.
Oxygen runs short, so unburned methane builds up, and methane is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so the hydrogen in methane escapes as poisonous hydrogen gas.

questions.explanation: Limited oxygen gives incomplete combustion. CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than O₂ does. It has no colour or smell.

questions.stem: Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of ethanol?
questions.explanation: In very limited O₂ the carbon is deposited as soot while the hydrogen still forms water. 3 O atoms in the products: 1 from ethanol, 2 from O₂.

questions.stem: Which pollutant in car exhaust forms from the air rather than from the fuel?
questions.explanation: Air is mostly N₂ and O₂. At the high temperature inside an engine they combine: N₂ + O₂ → 2NO. The fuel contains no nitrogen.
